Mirashi Bibi being dead her legal heirs: 1(a) Abdur Rouf and others ---- Appellants
vs
Amena Khatun and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque, J: This appeal has been preferred against the judgment and decree dated 30-8-1998 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) 1st Court, Brahmanbria in Title Suit No.16 of 1989 decreeing the suit in part. 

 2. The plaintiffs filed the suit for a decree of partition against the defendants claiming that the schedule property originally belonged to their predecessor Hazi Aminuddin Bepari who acquired the same by inheritance and by purchase in his own name and in the benami of his eldest son Shishu Mia. The plaintiffs, as heirs of Hazi Arninuddin are jointly entitled to get 13/16th share in the suit property, but the defendants have been possessing the land beyond their share, consequently, they demanded partition of the same on 3-5-1988, but the defendants refused, hence, the present suit for partition. 

 6. The trial court framed 4 (four) issues for determination of the dispute. In course of hearing both the parties examined witnesses in support of their respective cases and submitted bunch of documents major part of which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court after hearing by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-8-1998 decreed the suit in part in preliminary form allotting saham to the plaintiff for 20.09 acres. 

 7. Mr Sikder Mahmudur Razi, learned Advocate appearing for the Appellants submits that the trial court ought to have decreed the suit for 26.943/4 acres in favour of the plaintiffs, but decreed the suit in part allotting saham for 20.09 acres however, he candidly submits that the trial court rightly calculated the share of the respective parties and held that the deed of exchange executed and registered in between Shishu Mia and defendant No. 8 found to be in order as the plaintiff could not bring any evidence to disprove the deed of exchange. It is also argued that the trial court rightly observed that Shishu Mia acquired only 8.03 acres out of suit property and he can exchange the same, but instead of such quantum of land he exchanged 8.32 acres which was beyond his entitlement, resultantly, defendant No. 8 is entitled to get 8.03 acres, accordingly, the suit is decreed, but in the operative portion of the judgment the trial court failed to give any decision as to how the structures mentioned under schedule-9 should be disposed of. 

 9. He further submits that the plaintiffs though in the plaint claimed that Aminuddin purchased some land in the benami of his eldest son Shishu Mia, but did not pray for such declaration as well as could not prove the same by any evidence, as such, they cannot claim the property owned by Shishu Mia, but the trial court by consolidating all the property owned by Aminuddin and Shishu Mia gave saham to the plaintiff as prayed for, as such, the trial court has committed illegality in decreeing the Suit in Part. 

 10. Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, have gone through the grounds taken in appeal memo, plaint, written statement, evidences both oral and documentary available in lower court records and impugned judgment and decree of the trial court. 

 13. The trial court while decreeing the suit did not appreciate such aspect of the case and only on the averments made by the plaintiffs in the plaint and evidences led by them decreed the suit in their favour. 

 17. In the result, the appeal is allowed, judgment and decree of the trial court is hereby set-aside however, without any costs.
